#2868. The Unsung Performance of Baylor Scheierman

The Boston Celtics avoided another potential collapse of a 20-point lead last night, regaining their composure down the stretch to secure a 109–102 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks

Paul George and Derrick White spearheaded the effort, particularly in the closing minutes, while Neemias Queta also proved instrumental in the game's decisive moments. However, one player whose contributions I felt were particularly underrated throughout the contest was Baylor Scheierman.

Scheierman finished with nine points and 11 rebounds, including three on the offensive glass, while adding a steal and an assist in 28 minutes of action. Over his last three games, he has averaged 10 points and six rebounds while shooting an impressive 61% from beyond the arc.

Scheierman's impact also extended well beyond the box score. Here is a closer look at the various ways he influenced last night's game.

His impact began on the defensive end, where I thought he was particularly effective both on and off the ball. On this possession, he initially denies Herro an opportunity to receive the ball before rotating over to help on the drive, using an active swipe to force the pickup. When the ball eventually finds its way back to Herro, Scheierman stays disciplined, applies solid on-ball pressure, and closes out with a strong contest.

Here, Scheierman is matched up with Ryan Rollins, who prepares to use a wide screen from his big man, Kel'el Ware. Although Scheierman gets caught momentarily, he makes a smart adjustment by going under the screen, meeting Rollins at the other side, and recovering to get back in front. He then does a nice job staying attached through the subsequent on-ball screen, with some help from Luka Garza's hedge.

Once again, Scheierman showcases his off-ball activity by rotating over to help on another driving opponent. This time, however, we get a look at his instincts in the passing lanes. At the last moment, he reads the passer's intentions and peels back to his assignment to get a hand on the ball and deflect it.

Scheierman entered this game, averaging 4.6 deflections per 100 possessions, placing him in the 86th percentile league wide. His activity in this area makes him a valuable piece of a Celtics defense that ranks second in the NBA in deflections per game.

Garza ultimately gets the block on this next possession, but Scheierman made it possible. As the Bucks drive along the baseline, Mitchell Robinson, who is initially guarding Ware in the paint, is forced to rotate over and help on the ball. With Robinson leaving Ware, the big is momentarily left without a defender underneath the basket.

Scheierman recognizes this immediately and quickly sinks down toward Ware, reaching in an attempt to disrupt the pass. Although he doesn't come away with the steal, his presence forces Ware to adjust before going up for the layup. That split-second hesitation gives his teammates enough time to recover and get into position to contest the shot, ultimately setting up Garza's block.

Scheierman was credited with just one assist in this game, but his playmaking helped generate several quality looks for Boston. He finished with five potential assists on the night, and his ability to grab defensive rebounds and immediately push the pace (rip and run) continues to be an asset to the Celtics' early offense.

Scheierman attacks off the dribble and creates an opportunity for Robinson at the rim before quickly getting back on defense. He then does a nice job stepping in to cut off a driving lane and deter a potential three-point attempt, showcasing his ability to impact both ends of the floor in quick succession.

Staying on the offensive side of things, all nine of Scheierman's points came from downtown. He knocked down a three at the end of the half before quickly getting back on defense to contest a shot. Later, he connected on two big back-to-back threes that helped keep Milwaukee at bay.

On Rollins again here and he defends this "Iverson" cut perfectly. An Iverson cut is when a player uses two horizontal off ball screens to cut from one wing to the other.

He navigated both screens well and meets Rollins on the opposite wing, giving him no room to instantly drive. He then plays on the ball well and gets help from George who steals the pass and scores for the and one.

Anticipation and a quick reaction to the ball are obviously important traits for anyone looking to excel in the passing lanes defensively, but Scheierman has also shown an ability to incorporate deception into his approach. I first noticed this during the preseason and wanted to see another example before making the observation with confidence. This play provides exactly that.

Boston sends a double-team at Rollins near half court, forcing Scheierman into a Cover 2 situation. Watch how he deliberately leans his body toward the corner, giving the illusion that Ware is available for an easy pass in the paint. Rollins takes the bait, and Scheierman quickly changes direction to jump the passing lane and come away with the steal.

Another example of his off-ball prowess here getting another deflection.

Scheierman added several more quality possessions to the tape, giving the coaching staff plenty to be encouraged by.

Scheierman continued to make his presence felt in some of the game's biggest moments. His relentless pursuit of the basketball consistently puts him in position to make important hustle plays, and he has the skill and awareness to make those opportunities count.

He finds his way to the ball and gets his only true assist of the game to White for a huge and one then crashes for an offensive rebound that helped Boston wind down more time on the clock.

Lastly, we come back to the off-ball defense. On a play where the Bucks must get something, he communicates and performs three perfect switches before the ball is even entered.

Baylor Scheierman's impact in this game was a great example of how much value he can provide beyond the traditional box score. Whether it was his activity in the passing lanes, defensive positioning, ability to push the pace in transition, or timely shooting, he consistently found ways to positively impact the game.

Nine points and 11 rebounds are a solid contribution on their own, but his overall impact went well beyond those numbers. These are the types of winning plays that earn a coaching staff's trust, and Scheierman continues to make a strong case for a meaningful role in Boston's rotation.

#2865. Derrick White flipped the switch when the Celtics needed him

BOSTON — After the Celtics beat the Bucks, Derrick White sat in the locker room with ice packs on both knees and ice wrapped around his left shoulder.

The 32-year-old Celtics guard was coming off a season-high 24 points, plus 7 assists and 4 rebounds. He scored 11 points in the fourth quarter and 7 of the Celtics' final 10 points, including an and-one runner that gave the Celtics a 5-point lead with just over two minutes to go.

And, none of the late-game heroics were a surprise to his teammates.

"D-White just has an unwavering confidence — he just has a way of just being even-keeled," said Paul George, who led the Celtics in scoring with 25 on the night. "Obviously, he's great down the stretch."

This season, White is averaging 12.8 points, 5.1 assists, and 3.3 rebounds per game. For the second straight year, his shooting has slipped; he's shooting 42.5% from the field and 31% from three.

Regardless, for the second consecutive home game, White got raucous MVP chants at the free-throw line from the TD Garden. Afterward, he chatted with Jayson Tatum in the locker room, who donned street clothes after his first rest game of the season.

The two shared a laugh as White got ready to take the podium after his season-best game. Payton Pritchard exited the game in the third quarter after suffering a right eye abrasian, leaving the Celtics without two of their primary scorers in the clutch-time game against the Bucks.

That meant White knew he had to make a concerted effort offensively down the stretch.

"Every game is a little different — different lineups, different matchups, and so just kind of go out there, read what the game tells you to do, and go out there and compete, try to get a win," White said. "Obviously with JT out and then P going out too, had to [have] a little bit more aggressive mindset, and maybe next game is a little different. So, you just kind of go out there and have fun playing basketball."

The Celtics led by as many as 22 points in the game, but saw that lead turn into a one-point deficit late in the fourth quarter after a monster third quarter by Tyler Herro and multiple stints of offensive woes.

As the momentum of the game turned against Boston, White remained calm.

"He's a great defender, shot-blocker, rebounder at the guard spot — but again, with him, with Payton, like those guys just having kind of an even-keeled mentality, never get too high, never get too low, never really rattle," George said. "And when you're on the floor, you feel that you got a guy besides — he's obviously been a champion. So, he's tested. He's battle-tested. But to have someone that never gets too high, it's a level where I think when you're on the floor, you feel that, and you know, anything you're into, will get out of."

#2863. Thursday Night Football live updates, TV channel, stream, where to watch NFL game tonight

The Baltimore Ravens and Jacksonville Jaguars are heading in opposite directions as they prepare to square off on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 9.

But Baltimore's struggles have less to do with a lack of talent and more to do with a pair of injuries in their quarterback room. The biggest blow, of course, is the loss of two-time MVP Lamar Jackson, who has already missed three games this season and will now land on injured reserve (IR) after suffering a thumb injury that requires surgery.

Backup Tyler Huntley isn't riding to the rescue, either, after suffering a turf toe injury that will sideline him for the rest of the season.

That leaves undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to make his first NFL start. The former Maine and UConn quarterback put together an impressive college career, throwing for 10,926 yards and 94 touchdowns. Still, Thursday night will be quite the introduction to life in the NFL.

At 4-4, the Ravens aren't out of contention by any stretch, and they acquired veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals via trade on Weds. Nov. 4, though the trade will not be finalized until after tonight's game. The 33-year-old will not play in today's game but he brings stability to the position and should quickly assimilate in Baltimore upon arrival.

The visiting Jaguars, meanwhile, look like one of the AFC's emerging contenders. Their defense has been downright stingy against the run, becoming the first team since the 1970 merger to hold every opposing rusher under 40 yards through its first five games. Jacksonville has also extended its streak of not allowing a 75-yard rusher to 23 consecutive games. That's a daunting assignment for Ravens running back Derrick Henry.

Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence and head coach Liam Coen have the Jaguars' offense firing on all cylinders. Can Jacksonville make another statement in primetime, or will Fagnano and the Ravens stun everyone?

#2862. Ravens put Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley on IR; sign Austin Reed to active roster

Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are officially on the Ravens’ injured reserve list.

It’s been known for a few days that both quarterbacks were headed to the list and the moves were announced ahead of Thursday night’s game against the Jaguars. Huntley is going to miss the rest of the season with a toe injury and Jackson may be out for the rest of the year as well. He is set for surgery on his right thumb after being injured early in last Sunday’s loss to the Bills.

Huntley was injured a short time later, which led to Joe Fagnano’s regular season debut. He’ll make his starting debut against Jacksonville and Austin Reed will be on hand to back him up. Reed signed to the practice squad this week and the team announced that he’s now been signed to the active roster. They also signed Kedon Slovis off of the Packers’ practice squad this week.

The makeup of the quarterback room is set to change again next week. The Ravens are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals that will bring Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.

In addition to the quarterback moves, the Ravens also elevated kicker Jake Moody and linebacker Adisa Isaac from the practice squad for Thursday night.

#2861. Grading the Mavericks: Zaccharie Risacher’s reimagined role has been a key piece of Dallas’ success

The Mavericks went 3-2 over the last week-and-a-half, and sit at 4-4 overall. They won three in a row against Miami (113-109), Oklahoma City (120-96), and Houston (116-111). They have lost their last two against Sacramento (115-100) and San Antonio (112-111). Cooper Flagg led the team in scoring with 24.8 points per game.

Despite the sour taste that Cooper Flagg's last two games have left in everyone's mouths, the Mavericks deserve a good grade. They beat two great teams in the Thunder and Rockets, and a Miami team with multiple former All-Stars. For three games in a row, they looked like a playoff team. Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg's pairing made sense, P.J. Washington has been excellent all year, and Daniel Gafford has given Dallas a lot of what he gave them two years ago. Even Walter Clayton Jr., the 18th overall pick just last year, has given them a bright spot in a dark guard room.

Unfortunately, they tested fate by resting Irving on Monday against the Kings, and the basketball gods punished them by giving Sacramento their first win of the season in Dallas. The bad vibes continued for another two quarters, where the Mavericks got embarrassed in the first half against the Spurs. These six periods dropped them from an A+ to an A-. Luckily, they came out with energy in the second half and made what was looking like a stomping into a really exciting one-point loss against the defending Western Conference champions.

As previously mentioned, it is important to note how bad Cooper Flagg has looked in the last two games. He is just 10-of-38 (26.3 percent) from the floor, has not made a three, and has looked overwhelmingly disinterested on offense. Something doesn't look quite right, and they're going to need him to figure it out to take advantage of the next week of games.

Dallas has a three-game home stand against Brooklyn, Utah, and Indiana coming up.

Risacher was the first overall selection by Atlanta just three drafts ago. By no fault of his own, he was scrutinized for underperforming a draft placement he shouldn't have been taken at. When he was traded to Dallas, those expectations dissipated. It seems like a weight has been lifted from his shoulders, because Risacher has been one of the most important pieces to winning the Mavericks have.

He is just one of five players with 10+ steals and 10+ blocks this year. He is a legitimately good rebounder and has made threes sporadically. His commitment to defense has been enlightening, and his signature performance came this past week when he held Shai Gilgeous-Alexander to just 21 points on 7-of-19 shooting in a 24-point win. If Dallas is going to be a playoff team, Risacher will be in the rotation.

Yes, we are just eight games into his career. Yes, he was dealing with shin splints before the season. And yes, he was never supposed to be a flashy lottery pick. But it is impossible to ignore the tape that Morez Johnson Jr. has put together. Especially when Yaxel Lendeborg, his Michigan teammate, was picked after him and is averaging 21.5 points a game in Golden State.

Johnson Jr. was finally taken off a minutes restriction against the Spurs on Wednesday, and looked significantly more mobile. But for the majority of his minutes he has been a step slow, fouled a ton, and has given the Mavericks little to nothing on the offensive end. He is scoring just over seven points a game, grabbing just 3.1 rebounds, and fouling three times in his 16 minutes a night. Hopefully he can stack minutes as he ramps up, but he has been disappointing thus far.

It's taken a little bit of time, but Irving is starting to look like himself again. The paint touches are not quite there yet; it takes a lot of time to trust your legs to jump and move in traffic again. But the three-point shot looks good, he is moving well laterally, and he is digging in on rebounds and the defensive end. He's coming off back-to-back games of 35 and 29 points, and although the latter was not super efficient, he is starting to score in bunches like he did pre-injury. It is only a matter of time where he is doing things again that leave us in awe.

#2859. Patriots re-sign veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor to practice squad

A veteran of 85 NFL games has returned to Gillette Stadium to fill the open spot on the practice squad.

The New England Patriots officially re-signed cornerback Kindle Vildor to the 17-man scout team on Thursday after he had been released from the 53-man roster earlier in the week.

Vildor, 28, first made his way to Foxborough on a one-year contract as an unrestricted free agent in March. The 5-foot-11, 190-pound vested corner intercepted a pass in preseason action before beginning the regular season on the practice squad. After serving as a standard elevation for the 29-26 AFC East upset of the Buffalo Bills, he was promoted to the active roster and earned a game ball from head coach Mike Vrabel following the 45-17 rout of the Las Vegas Raiders.

In all, Vildor has appeared in five games this fall while notching seven tackles, including one for loss, as well as one forced fumble and one pass deflection. His stay spans 53 snaps on defense to go with 32 snaps on special teams.

New England currently carries Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis III, Marcus Jones, Charles Woods, Channing Canada and Karon Prunty on the active cornerback depth chart, while the midweek re-signing joins Al'zillion Hamilton on the practice squad.

Entering the NFL with the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall, Vildor has also made stops with Tennessee Titans, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. A 27-game starter during his time in the league, the Georgia Southern product has recorded 147 tackles, one sack, two forced fumbles and two interceptions through 2,158 snaps on defense and 605 snaps on special teams.

After safety Elliott Davison cleared waivers and circled back, one spot remained vacant on the practice squad.

The Green Bay Packers visit Gillette Stadium on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

#2858. Milwaukee Bucks NBA 2K27 simulation: Part 2

There were some wild outcomes in our first NBA 2K simulation, an AI-controlled affair that offered a glimpse of what could happen for the Milwaukee Bucks this season. Some outcomes were fun to see, some were not, and some were… tragically ironic (sorry, Scoot). This time, let's take a look at a more realistic simulation of how the Bucks' season might turn out. I'll be setting the lineups and player minutes—and trying to pull off some roster moves that I think would be realistic and beneficial for the Bucks.

The season begins with the Bucks clearing their roster issues: waiving Kevin Porter Jr., Johni Broome, Jake Stephens, and Pete Nance before welcoming back Nance on a two-way contract. That leaves their starting lineup looking exactly as it did for Taylor Jenkins and the real Bucks (save for the reversal of the forward positions):

Amid early-season play, the Bucks are twice ranked 21st in the power rankings and once 22nd. The way things are going in real life, I'm sure Bucks fans wouldn't be too mad to see this.

Roster-wise, the Bucks have Myles Turner, Caris LeVert, Gary Trent Jr., and Kyle Kuzma all on the trading block. On the flipside, Kasparas Jakučionis, Brayden Burries, and Nate Ament—a young core trio that Bucks will be looking to hold and develop over the next few years—are set as their untouchables.

In December, Milwaukee sits 7-24 on the season. One of the "leading" factors in this has been Myles Turner, who has been horrible, scoring just 7.9 PPG on 33% from the field (Editor's note: So, pretty true to life?). On a better note, Kel'el Ware looks great and has been averaging a double-double off the bench. As such, he will move into the starting position in a bid to improve the team's 27th-ranked rebounding.

TRADE ALERT: The Milwaukee Bucks are sending AJ Green and Jericho Sims to the Denver Nuggets for Marvin Bagley III, Zeke Nnaji and a 2028 second-round pick.

The Nuggets, short on options at the two-guard position, make the trade for Dairy Bird with the intention of improving their second-to-last in the league ranking in three-point attempts. Meanwhile, the Bucks acquire Bagley, who is having a strong season, averaging 10.6 PPG and 8.8 RPG on 56% shooting from the field, to bolster the big rotation. In Naji, they also add a theoretical scoring boost at power forward, a skill Jericho Sims has been unable to provide. More importantly, Milwaukee adds to its draft chest.

The Bucks roll into the All-Star Break with an 18-41 record, showing improvement after their slow start to the season. Despite starting to turn his season around, Turner remains a prominent name on the trade block; unfortunately, nothing comes together for the Bucks, even with Kristaps Porzingis, Miles Bridges, and Rui Hachimura all being floated for him. It has, however, been made clear that Turner's name will still be in trade talks come the offseason.

On a more positive note, Jakučionis makes the World Team for the Rising Star Game, averaging 10.8 PPG, 3.1 RPG, and 3.2 APG. He doesn't lead the Bucks in any category, though. Those honours go to:

As a team, the Bucks are the 28th-ranked offence in the league, with 109.6 PPG. Their defence is better, though, ranking 19th in the league (giving up 121.4 PPG). It's not quite the "Bad Boy Bucks" that fans have been hoping for, but definitely a step in the right direction in the Bucks' quest to become a defensive-minded team. As for power rankings, Taylor Jenkins' team hovers between 26th and 27th, a regression from the start of the season despite their improved play. Looking at the standings, Milwaukee sits 13th in the Eastern Conference and 25th overall.

Down the stretch, the Bucks improve slightly, finishing as the 27th-ranked offence with 110.6 PPG. Their defence fares better, ranking 19th overall, despite giving up 121.2 PPG. As far as the standings go, Milwaukee finishes 26-56 and in the 13th position in the Eastern Conference—a very realistic outcome and probably a spot where Bucks fans wouldn't be too mad to finish. On a positive note, Brayden Burries makes the All-Rookie Second Team, averaging 6.9 PPG, 1.3 RPG, and 0.8 APG. It's a pleasing accomplishment for Burries, even if the numbers are underwhelming. And on that note, the Bucks statistical leaders end up as:

On the night of the NBA draft, the Bucks are looking to make a trade and still Turner's name is ringing hot in front offices around the league. Yes, even after another down season, teams are looking to take a swing on him.

The phone rings. It's the Portland Trail Blazers…

BREAKING NEWS: The Portland Trail Blazers are trading the 20th overall pick in the 2027 NBA Draft to the Milwaukee Bucks for Myles Turner and the 45th pick in the draft.

The Trail Blazers make the move believing they are one piece away from being a top-3 contender in the Western Conference, and feel strongly that the twin towers of Myles Turner and Donovan Clingan are going to be the key to getting past the dominant bigs of the West, like Victor Wembanyama and Chet Holmgren.

With the pick, the Bucks select Babatunde Oladotun, a 6'10", lengthy, high-upside forward out of Maryland. But the surprises don't end there. In one of the biggest draft-day falls, the Bucks pick up 7'3" center Luigi Suigo out of Villanova. Suigo was projected to be a lottery pick earlier in the year, but it seems questions regarding his cardio and frame began to swirl around the league, enabling the Bucks to take a swing on the big man with the 35th pick.

Following the draft, the Bucks exercise the team options on both Ware and Jakučionis to kick off their free agency period. They then re-sign Jaquez, Herro, and Rollins to new contracts. They also add Jalen Smith and Santi Aldama on cheap deals to add some more size to their lineup following the Turner trade.

Along with the additions, the Bucks say goodbye to fan favourite Kuzma, veteran Caris LeVert, and two-way players Cormac Ryan and Kam Jones. Heading into the 2027-2028 season, the starting lineup thus looks like this:

Overall, this certainly isn't as blockbuster as the AI-controlled simulation, but I feel like it is a better look at a realistic outcome: retaining the Bucks' core and adding some key pieces to raise the team's floor.

So, did this 2K simulation tickle your fancy, or was it a fever dream a little too close to reality? Be sure to share your thoughts in the comments.

#2855. Brian Schottenheimer says 2 Cowboys starters still in concussion protocol ahead of Week 9

A Cowboys defensive backfield that has been victimized repeatedly over the first eight games of the 2026 season could find itself once again stretched thin and scrambling to fill spots when the team travels to Indianapolis for their Week 9 matchup.

Wednesday's practice report listed 11 Cowboys players as either non-participants or limited in the day's work session. And while the impact of various injuries has been felt up and down the roster, the Cowboys are notably hurting in the secondary, with both first-round rookie Caleb Downs and veteran P.J. Locke currently in the league's concussion protocol following last weekend's 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona.

Both starters were on the practice field for workouts on Wednesday, but neither took part in drills. On Thursday, both were in full pads, a promising step. According to head coach Brian Schottenheimer, though, the team has been exploring backup options for Sunday's tilt with the Colts.

"We've got some guys on the practice squad that we could elevate," Schottenheimer said in his Wednesday press conference. "Both those guys are doing good today, but there's a long process, obviously. But we've got some things in place, some guys that have experience playing both nickel and safety that we could move around."

Either would be a major loss for Dallas. Downs has played 92% of the defense's snaps so far this season. Locke's usage has been far spottier. He played sparingly in the season opener and then exited Week 2's game after just three snaps with a torn plantar fascia. After sitting out the next five games, he saw 84% of the unit's snaps against the Cardinals before leaving late in the overtime period.

Also on this week's watchlist are cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was fully involved Wednesday but has been dealing with a nagging ankle injury, and safety Jalen Thompson, who suffered a hamstring injury back in Week 3 and is still awaiting the opening of his 21-day practice window. At this point, it seems very unlikely Thompson would be ready to take the field in Week 9.

"Not yet," Schottenheimer said on that potential development.

Replacing Downs and Locke in the Dallas lineup this week could mean another opportunity for Reddy Steward. The third-year man has already been elevated from the practice squad three times (versus Baltimore, Houston, and Tampa Bay) and would have to be added to the 53-man roster in order to play again. Juanyeh Thomas is another name to keep an eye on. While he has plenty of past experience as a safety, the vast majority of his usage since rejoining the club in October has come on special teams.

Malik Hooker, Markquese Bell, and Alijah Clark are the Cowboys' remaining safeties. Hooker has played over 60% of the unit's snaps in each game since Week 4, when he returned from a fractured forearm. Bell saw just three defensive snaps last week- filling in for Locke- but was on the field for as much as 80% of the defense's action during Locke's previous absence. Clark is a special teams staple but did log 40 defensive snaps in the Cowboys' visit to Philadelphia in Week 7.

As a defense, the Cowboys are allowing 232.6 passing yards per game, a mark that's 11th-worst in the NFL through eight games. Only four units have given up more explosive pass plays than Dallas's 27.

This week they'll face the Colts, who rank 28th leaguewide in passing yards per game, with 174.6.

#2852. What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique

What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

They're a team of superstars that don't play superstar basketball.

That's the beauty of this 76ers team. They play a brand of unselfish team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars.

LeBron James is one of the two or three greatest players in NBA history, a four-time MVP, a four-time NBA champion, a 1st-ballot Hall of Famer.

Joel Embiid is a seven-time all-star, a former MVP, an Olympic gold medalist and a likely Hall of Famer.

Jaylen Brown is a five-time all-star, an NBA champion, a career 20 points-per-game scorer.

Tyrese Maxey is a two-time all-star, one of only two NBA guards averaging 27.0 points per game over the last four years.

Four certified megastars on one team. And somehow they've figured out how to leave their egos at the front door and play smart, tough, disciplined team basketball, the style of ball you just never see on these superstar-laden teams.

On offense, they patiently work the ball around, always looking for the open man or a positive matchup. You've got this bunch of big-name, high-priced All-Stars who are just as happy to pass the ball as shoot it. That never happens.

The 76ers are sixth in the NBA in assists, and they're one of only four teams with twice as many assists as turnovers. Smart, unselfish, patient, disciplined.

When an all-timer like LeBron averages 7.3 assists per game that speaks volumes. LeBron is fifth in the NBA in assists per game among forwards, which is wild. You can see the joy on his face when one of his passes leads to a basket. When one of the greatest players in history has that mentality, it rubs off on everyone around him.

Embiid hasn't really got going yet on offense and still takes too many 3's, but he's also embraced the team-first mentality, and his 4.8 assists per game are more than one full assist above his career average and 4th-most in the NBA among centers or forward-centers. And still one of the most dominating defensive players in the league.

Brown is averaging 27.0 points, which you expect, but he's also averaging 4.3 assists per game, significantly above his career average of 3.8 coming into the season. He's fit in so well so fast you forget its his first season here.

And what can you even say about Maxey? Just a beast. He's averaging nearly 30 points per game but never wastes a possession, always makes the right decision with the ball in his hands and is still finding time to average 4.3 assists per game.

With James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey, the 76ers are the only NBA team with four guys averaging at least 16 points and 4 assists per game. Only the Pacers, Magic and Raptors have three.

But where we're really seeing this group playing out of their minds is on the defensive end, where this bunch of all-stars, including two newcomers, has been astounding.

The 76ers have the 2nd-best defensive efficiency rating in the league, behind only the Pistons, who they play Wednesday night, and they're allowing the 2nd-fewest points in the league, also behind Detroit. Last year, they allowed 123 points per game through eight games. This year they're at 111.

They're holding teams to 43 percent shooting from the field, 3rd-best in the league and their lowest since 2011-12. Their 9.3 steals per game are 6th-most.

All five starters are among the top 25 players in the league in defensive rating – James is fourth, Embiid 11th, Edgecombe 15th, Maxey 22nd and Brown 23rd. How is that even possible?

It's rare to see superstar-caliber guys play as hard on the defensive end as the offensive end. Everybody on this team embraces it. They hustle, they work, they communicate and most importantly they commit to it.

The biggest concern when the 76ers built this dream team was that it would be a team of individuals out for themselves, but the reality has been the opposite.

In a very short period of time, they've learned how to play together. How to play for each other.

And we haven't even mentioned V.J. Edgecomb, who at 21 years old has figured out how to assimilate into this loaded lineup, never force anything, wait for his opportunities and make huge shots when he gets his turn. Edgecombe is at 12.7 points and 3.0 assists per game, and his numbers are understandably down a bit from last year, but if that bothers him it sure doesn't show.

And the role players – Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jabari Walker – have each adopted the same ego-free style of basketball, supporting the starters however they need to.

Nick Nurse deserves a ton of credit for getting this bunch to play this brand of hoops. It's not easy to get any NBA player to put team goals ahead of individual goals. But he's got Hall of Famers and all-stars doing it and having a blast along the way. They all seem to love playing basketball the right way and they seem to love playing together.

The 76ers are 7-1 and looking like a real threat to win the East, and they're doing it by playing the game the right way.

By committing to each other and not themselves.

#2847. Is Tosh Lupoi in trouble at Cal? Ron Rivera just turned up the heat

Tosh Lupoi's first season as a head coach hasn't been ideal on the field. His general manager Ron Rivera, a former NFL head coach, gave a harsh review of how things are going at Cal on Thursday, Nov. 5.

Cal has been one of the worst teams in the ACC this season, holding a 3-6 record with a 2-4 mark in conference play. Its offense has taken a step back despite returning talented quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, with Lupoi even stripping Jordan Sommerville of play-calling duties in favor of Pat McCann against UNLV on Oct. 6.

College football picks: Predictions for every Top 25 game on Week 10 schedule

Rivera emphasized in his weekly radio appearance with "The Sports Leader" that Lupoi, the former Oregon defensive coordinator, is still learning as a first-time head coach, but that the program needs to start going "north" with four games left in the regular season.

"He has bumped his head a lot," Rivera said. "We have talked a lot, tried to give him a lot of advice, point him in the right direction. Some of it, he's been very receptive, and other portions of it, he hasn't. And it's those things that sometimes you've gotta learn for yourself before you think, 'Oh wow, this is it.' But I'd like to continue to stress that this is a guy that's learning, growing. But now it's time.

"These last three games, hopefully four, the trajectory has to be going north. We have to show that we are growing, there has been some growth and development of our players, our team, and the culture is getting stronger. Those are all things that you have to have going forward."

Cal was dominated by nearby UCLA 45-24 in Week 1 in a matchup between first-year coaches — Lupoi and UCLA's Bob Chesney — and former Pac-12 rivals. The Bruins are now 8-0, while the Bears are 3-6.

The directions in which both programs are trending doesn't help the cause, either, although Rivera offered an explanation of why the two comparable programs are on different footings.

"The biggest thing I can tell you guys is — again, I know expectations were very, very high, and I know there's the comparison to UCLA, but the thing everybody's gotta understand is UCLA brought in a current head coach that came and brought probably half of the team that he had that went to the playoff to begin with," Rivera said. "Tosh came in as a first-time head coach. He did bring a couple of inexperienced coordinators with him. Things didn't work out the way we needed them to work out on offense."

Like Rivera said, the offense has been a problem at times. Sagapolutele has battled injuries but has taken a step back this season as a sophomore, ranking 88th of 138 starting quarterbacks nationally with a 48.4 QBR.

Cal needs to win its final three games to reach bowl eligibility, which is possible with remaining games against winnable opponents in Virginia, Stanford and Pittsburgh.

But if things fall off the tracks too far, perhaps Lupoi's job status will become a question mark after only a season at the helm.

"We've got to get this foundation put down, we've got to show that we have solid roots in the ground, we are ready to go forward," Rivera said. "Then we can hit the recruiting trail being able to point to the direction, saying, 'Look, we're heading north. We're doing the things that we need to do. We're putting the players in position, so let's roll.' And that's what we have to do."

#2846. Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double

Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season.

Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.

On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards.

The Sixers' absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team's matchup with the Pistons on Sunday.

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory Saturday:

Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James' place. He'd missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

The 3-and-D forward scored the night's first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession.

Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team's offense in the early going.

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man.

Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead.

One of Embiid's assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter.

The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn't enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter.

Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run.

Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn't carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly.

Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins' three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead.

The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they'd fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win.

The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team's transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game's first 19 fast-break points.

The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup.

Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup.

Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks' odds of a road win. They'd all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter.

Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers' lead to 97-87.

The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel'el Ware's put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee's deficit to 117-114.

The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure.

For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

#2844. Bill Belichick nominated for Pro Football Hall of Fame 2027 class after first-ballot snub

The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced coach nominees for the Class of 2027 on Nov. 5, with Belichick headlining the list of five. It marks the second consecutive season for the former New England Patriots head coach, who oversaw one of the greatest dynasties in NFL history.

Belichick's snub on the first ballot sparked outrage across the football world in January, leaving many to question the Hall of Fame's voting process. Now the path to enshrinement in Canton, Ohio, looks a little different as sweeping changes were enacted in September.

The Hall slashed its voting body from 50 members to 25 as part of the change. It will also have three non-voting members that will make up a 28-person selection committee. The three non-voters are set to rotate each season.

JARRETT BELL: I'm a Pro Football Hall of Fame voter. We blew it with Bill Belichick snub | Opinion

Subcommittees initially debated a list of 14 coaching candidates for enshrinement in 2027 before settling on the list of five that includes Belichick, Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan.

All five nominees found themselves in the same position last year, with Belichick being chosen as the category's representative.

And, just like last year, only one will advance out of the group again to be among the 15 finalists that will include 13 modern-era Players, one coach and one contributor.

Belichick didn't receive the necessary votes for induction as part of the Class of 2026. Under the previous voting rules, the coach would've needed at least 40 of 50 votes to be enshrined in Aug. 2026.

Since voting for the Pro Football Hall of Fame isn't public, it's unclear how many votes Belichick received.

Belichick spoke about the snub during an interview with Fox News' Sean Hannity on the May 19 episode of the "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast.

"Well, it's out of my control," Belichick said. "And honestly, I've been very focused on my job at the University of North Carolina and the players and the university there. So, you know, whatever happens, happens. But I'm proud of what we accomplished as teams at New England and certainly at the Giants, and proud of those relationships. So that's what matters most."

Belichick said appreciated the outpouring of support for his Hall of Fame case in the immediate aftermath of the 2026 snub.

"It's great to hear that support from so many people and from so many different fields – not just football, but many others," he added. "And so, you know, I was very appreciative of that support and the positive comments that they made."

Belichick wasn't willing to speculate on why he wasn't voted in, saying you'd have to ask the voters.

Belichick headlines the list of coach nominees for enshrinement as part of the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027. The Hall provided a brief bio on each as part of the announcement:

Bill Belichick: NFL coach from 1975-2023 with head coaching jobs with the Cleveland Browns (1991-95) and New England Patriots (2000-2023). Career record: 333-178 (including playoffs) with six Super Bowl titles as a head coach and two others as an assistant.

Tom Coughlin: Spent 20 years as an NFL head coach with the Jacksonville Jaguars (1995-2002) and New York Giants (2004-2015). Including playoffs, posted a 182-157 record and led the Giants to two Super Bowl titles. Also won a title with Giants as an assistant coach.

Mike Holmgren: Head coach of the Green Bay Packers from 1992-98 and the Seattle Seahawks from 1999-2008; won a Super Bowl ring in two Super Bowl trips with the Packers and appeared in another Super Bowl as head coach of the Seahawks. Career record: 174-122 (including postseason). Also won two Super Bowls as an assistant with the San Francisco 49ers.

Dan Reeves: Head coach of the Denver Broncos (1981-1992), New York Giants (1993-96) and Atlanta Falcons (1997-2003). Career record: 201-174-2 (including postseason). Led Broncos (three times) and Falcons (once) to the Super Bowl. Won a title as an assistant with the Dallas Cowboys.

Mike Shanahan: Head coach of the Los Angeles Raiders (1988-89), Denver Broncos (1995-2008) and Washington Redskins (2010-13). Won back-to-back Super Bowls with the Broncos while compiling a 178-144 career record (including playoffs). Also won a title with the San Francisco 49ers as an assistant coach.

Given Belichick's snub last year, it would appear likely that the voting body would avoid a repeat this time around. That would seemingly make the coach a heavy favorite to be inducted.

The Hall announced the list of contributor nominees on Nov. 4, which is headlined by Patriots owner Robert Kraft. Like Belichick, Kraft fell short of receiving the necessary votes for induction in 2026.

Here's a look at the full list of nominees, with the bios provided by the Hall:

Ralph Hay: Owned the Canton Bulldogs from 1918-1922; hosted the NFL's formational meeting in his automobile dealership in downtown Canton.

Robert Kraft: Owner of the New England Patriots since 1994 and chairman and CEO of the Kraft Group. His teams have won six Super Bowls and played in five others – 11 appearances overall in the past 31 seasons. Also key member of several influential NFL owners' committees.

Virginia McCaskey: Principal owner of the Chicago Bears from 1983 until her passing in 2025 at age 102. Daughter of team founder George Halas. During her tenure the Bears won Super Bowl XX during a stretch of five consecutive division titles.

Doug Williams: Nine-year NFL career was punctuated with a Super Bowl title and game MVP honors following a 340-yard, four-touchdown performance against the Broncos to cap the 1987 season. Has spent the past 13 seasons in the front office of the Commanders' franchise. Other stints as a scout or front office executive in the NFL came with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

John Wooten: An offensive lineman in the NFL for 10 seasons, he transitioned to scouting and player personnel roles with the Cowboys, Eagles and Ravens for nearly three decades. In 2003, became chair of the Fritz Pollard Alliance, a group working to advance opportunities for minorities in coaching and front office positions across pro football.

#2843. Joe Brady on cutting S C.J. Gardner-Johnson: "It was the best interests of the football team"

On the day the NFL suspended former Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for spitting on an opponent, Buffalo coach Joe Brady said the team would not be cutting Gardner-Johnson. After the game that Gardner-Johnson missed, the Bills cut him.

Meeting with reporters on Thursday, Brady explained the reversal.

“There was a lot to evaluate,” Brady said. “You know, we got together and figured out, ‘Hey, this is what we felt like this was the best thing to do for the Buffalo Bills.’ I have so much love for [C.J.]. Like, I really do. I loved getting to coach him. I loved being around him. I loved — I did love the edge, and his personality allowing him to be him, right?, and as a person. So that didn’t make the decision easy at all.

“But we also have to be an organization that, you know, it’s unfortunate obviously what happened, you know? But it also opened a door and an opportunity for guys the other day, and that was a part of evaluation. And seeing how those guys kind of played, and you know with a lot of the roster moves. And, again, this wasn’t — we didn’t come out of the game post Vegas and say, ‘This is what we were going to do. We’re just gonna do this the following Monday.’ We were, you know, the plan was him being here and we were going to evaluate it after the game in Baltimore. And we felt like with some of the moving parts we had to do it was the best interests of the football team.”

Gardner-Johnson’s suspension opened the door for Damar Hamlin to start the game against the Ravens. And Hamlin apparently did well enough to help the Bills realize that, all things considered, the “best interests” of the Bills meant the Bills were better off without the “high maintenance” Gardner-Johnson.

#2842. Clemson freshman quarterback talks learning on the fly with game time

Tait Reynolds once stepped onto a high school football field thinking of himself primarily as a baseball player. A few years later, he is leading Clemson's offense and coming off a performance that showed how much he is growing into the job.

The route between those moments has required Reynolds to adjust quickly. His latest challenge has been learning to run a college offense while facing the weekly demands of being a true freshman starter.

Against Florida State, that development produced encouraging results. Reynolds threw for 189 yards and two touchdowns, adding 89 rushing yards and another score in Clemson's 36-24 victory. His late 79-yard touchdown run secured the win and established a program record for the longest run by a quarterback.

"I just have some games under my belt," Reynolds said. "There's just that constant growth. You get a little more experience. The more experience, you get better and better. I think that is the biggest thing. You get a little more confident, comfortable."

Reynolds wasn't assured that experience entering the season. Fourth-year quarterback Christopher Vizzina was expected to take over, but Reynolds moved into the starting role after two games.

An unexpected opening also shaped his career at Queen Creek in Arizona. Reynolds began his first high school game at cornerback, covering Ja'Kobi Lane despite knowing little about the receiver and being more focused on baseball.

At halftime, his coaches put him at quarterback. Less than two years later, he committed to Clemson.

Now five starts into his college career, Reynolds has another opportunity to build momentum when the Tigers visit Syracuse. Offensive coordinator Chad Morris has emphasized that the difficult moments are part of that process.

"Coach Morris talks about it all the time. You can't skip these steps, and you have to go through these hard times, and you have to go through these trials. I think the more I play, the better I am going to get."

For Clemson, turning that experience into consistent production will be the next step, starting with Saturday's trip to Syracuse.

#2841. The Packers are asking Jordan Love to do something historically difficult

Jordan Love is putting together one of the best seasons of his career. That's good timing, because the Packers aren't making things particularly easy on him.

Through eight games, Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards and has thrown 16 touchdowns. He's on pace for a franchise-record 4,772 passing yards, potentially surpassing Aaron Rodgers' 2011 season. But there's a caveat: Love is being asked to overcome problems that few quarterbacks could reasonably be expected to sustain.

The Packers are averaging just 60.6 rushing yards per game, the lowest mark in the NFL over the past decade. They're also responsible for 23 dropped passes, eight more than any other team.

Against Carolina, Green Bay managed just 66 rushing yards on 26 carries. Opposing defenses continue to make Love beat them through the air. So far, he has. His development into a quarterback capable of carrying an offense is encouraging, and the team's 5-3 record reflects that resilience.

But there's a difference between having a quarterback who can overcome adversity and building an offense that consistently puts him in that position. The Packers don't need Love to do more. They need the rest of the offense to do more for him.

Unfortunately not much! The trade deadline is approaching, and I suppose there's a possibility that the Packers acquire a new running back. But given the run blocking the team has displayed this year, how much difference might a better back make? Speaking of the line, it's possible that their run blocking could improve and that could alleviate some of the issues. But don't hold your breath there. As for pass catchers… anyone can receive a pass, but it's catching of the pass. That's the key. Can the Packers receivers turn that around?

In the meantime, I'm choosing to simply marvel at the fact that, through 8 games, Jordan Love seems entirely capable of keeping me entertained on Sundays. It's extremely impressive given the circumstances, and that will have to do.

#2831. Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1

Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers kept up their hot start to the season Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, reaching 7-1 with a 126-107 win against the Bulls.

All five of the Sixers' starters scored in double figures. Tyrese Maxey posted 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown tallied a season-best 25 points and 11 rebounds.

VJ Edgecombe's 21 points were a new season high. LeBron James recorded 15 points, nine assists and seven boards.

Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson had 24 points and seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid (15 points, eight rebounds) had been listed as questionable with an official designation of "right foot plantar fascia injury management." He sat out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back for the Sixers' win over the Hornets.

"Plantar is a little bit of a come and go type of thing," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters pregame. "They're just trying to manage it. It's very painful, if you've ever had it. It can kind of come and go out of nowhere. So we're just trying to manage the pain with that, be as smart as we can."

Nurse told reporters that Dominick Barlow is set to see a specialist Tuesday about the back injury that's sidelined him to start the season.

"He's been on court a little bit … not a ton of moving around," Nurse said. "I think they want to get to tomorrow's appointment. Hopefully, it'll be positive and we can get into his workouts a little bit."

The Sixers will begin a three-game road trip Wednesday when they visit the Pistons. Here are observations on their victory Monday:

After Embiid blitzed a Bulls pick-and-roll, Maxey picked off Matas Buzelis' hurried pass to get the Sixers rolling in transition and James jammed home the team's first field goal.

Edgecombe got a slam soon after James grabbed a defensive rebound and the Sixers again pushed the pace. The Sixers scored six quick fast-break points, leading the Bulls to burn an early timeout, and James' long-distance feeds were a major asset.

"If you're open, he's going to pass it," Edgecombe said of James. "The main thing is just being ready. Tonight I had to run and go get 'em. If you're open and he sees you, he's going to pass the ball."

Edgecombe had a dunk-heavy first quarter. He threw down his second when Dean Wade nabbed a steal and dropped off a typically selfless dish to the Sixers' explosive second-year guard, whose slam put the team up 22-13.

The Sixers have an abundance of dangerous options in the open floor, Edgecombe included. As he's already shown with his continued clutch shotmaking, the 21-year-old won't become anything resembling a non-factor offensively this year as a byproduct of the Sixers' enhanced star power.

Over the team's first seven games, Edgecombe had averaged 11.3 points. He scored 11 in the first period on 5-for-5 shooting.

Adem Bona missed a dunk early in the second quarter, which stung a bit more when Jalen Smith drilled a three-pointer seconds later.

Bona remained the Sixers' main backup center. He had a poor first-half stint overall amid a largely negative start to his third season. The 23-year-old big man played well in the Sixers' victory over the Bucks, posting six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Outside of that, his season has been sparse on bright moments so far. It's reasonable to wonder when Nurse might turn to alternatives like Jabari Walker, who played a good game Saturday in Charlotte, or try James again at the five.

The Bulls outscored the Sixers by eight points in Bona's first run, cutting their derficit to 40-38. Chicago went in front with a three by former Sixer Buddy Hield.

The Sixers regained the advantage late in the second quarter. Maxey and James each were excellent as passers in the first half, combining for 14 assists and three turnovers. James fired the ball to Wade for a corner three that gave the Sixers a 60-52 lead.

Following a third-quarter Embiid fadeaway jumper and two James lay-ins, the Sixers were up 17 points.

The Bulls cut the Sixers' lead down to 11 points by the start of the fourth quarter. With Bona still struggling and on four fouls, Wade began the fourth at center. Bona then briefly spelled Wade before being whistled for his fifth foul and taking a seat. Embiid ultimately wasn't needed for any of the fourth period and only logged 25 minutes.

Embiid said postgame that he was not available to return to the action in the fourth and has been feeling his plantar fasciitis on the court. The seven-time All-Star's health is clearly not close to 100 percent.

"I was on a minutes restriction," he said. "(The foot) has been going like that for the past few weeks. It's painful. Just got to manage it.

"If it flares up pretty bad, got to take a step back. We've been able to manage it, but it has its ups and downs."

The Sixers' lead got as low as eight points, but Chicago did not shoot well enough from three-point range (26.3 percent) or have sufficient firepower to sustain a meaningful comeback run. The bottom line is the Sixers are in a different class than the Bulls, who fell to 1-6.

As for the Sixers, they'll wake up Tuesday morning at the top of the Eastern Conference standings.

"You've got some of these nights where you kind of call them professional wins. …You look at the records and all that kind of stuff, but they have a lot of talent," Nurse said. "A lot of these teams play a way that's a little scary. It's fast and it's furious, lots of threes. … They're going to keep coming at you, high-possession games. So they're not easy games and I'm glad that we handled it professionally tonight."

#2829. Seahawks’ Latest QB Move Could Signal Bigger Jalen Milroe Role

LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Adrian Martinez #4 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before a game before a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) Getty

SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks looks on against the Los Angeles Chargers at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty

The Seattle Seahawks added a quarterback Wednesday, and the move could give Jalen Milroe more time to prepare for a potential moment in the sun.

Seattle signed Adrian Martinez to its practice squad Nov. 4 with Sam Darnold ruled out against the Arizona Cardinals and Drew Lock managing an elbow injury.

According to Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR, the addition could help Milroe concentrate on Seattle's game plan while the team manages Lock's throwing workload.

GettyLAS VEGAS, NEVADA – AUGUST 27: Adrian Martinez #4 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before a game before a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images)

Milroe normally runs the scout-team offense, helping Seattle's defense prepare by imitating the opposing quarterback. Getting him ready to operate the Seahawks' own offense creates competing demands on his practice time.

Martinez's arrival gives Seattle another quarterback to handle that work.

"Or it may mean Milroe can just focus on Seattle's plays in practices to help manage Lock's reps," Bell wrote in his Nov. 4 report.

Bell noted that Seattle handled Darnold's previous absence differently. When Lock started against Arizona in Week 2, the Seahawks did not add another quarterback. Milroe prepared for Seattle's offensive game plan while also running the scout team.

The latest signing could ease that balancing act at a time when Seattle is preparing both Lock and Milroe to play.

Martinez also brings familiarity with the offensive system. As Seahawks.com noted, he previously spent time with the San Francisco 49ers, where Seattle offensive coordinator Brian Fleury worked before joining the Seahawks.

GettySEATTLE, WASHINGTON – OCTOBER 04: Jalen Milroe #6 of the Seattle Seahawks looks on against the Los Angeles Chargers at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images)

Lock remains the expected starter for Sunday, Nov. 8, at Lumen Field. Milroe's increased preparation comes as Seattle works through uncertainty about Lock's elbow.

"They'll be splitting reps for a certain amount of time," head coach Mike Macdonald said Wednesday, per Seahawks.com.

Lock was Seattle's inactive emergency third quarterback in each of the past two games, with Milroe serving as Darnold's backup. Macdonald said Lock can throw, but the team will manage how much he does throughout the week.

Darnold is considered week-to-week with a quad injury, and Seattle does not plan to place him on injured reserve.

The change for Milroe is more preparation with Seattle's offense. Whether that leads to game action will depend on how the quarterback situation develops before and during Sunday's matchup.

#2826. ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers

'I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jaylen Brown has spent the opening weeks of the season describing the Sixers as a work in progress.

He offered a similarly humble perspective Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. His performance, however, provided the clearest look yet at how he can influence this group while sharing the floor with the club's other established stars.

Brown finished with 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists in the Sixers' 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls. He shot 9 for 15 from the field, made four three-pointers and did not commit a turnover.

Five of his rebounds came on the offensive end, an area Brown has emphasized while the Sixers continue piecing together their frontcourt rotation.

"Just a mindset," Brown said. "Just trying to create extra opportunities for my team. As we're trying to patch together our fives and our front line, I try to make an extra contribution and emphasis on the glass."

Brown has also been careful about how he describes his place on a roster that already belonged to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter Monday, continuing his torrid start to the season. He has led the Sixers in scoring while being the only starter to appear in all eight games.

Brown is not interested in interrupting that.

"Maxey's been leading the way, 100 percent," Brown said. "He's been here. This is his team. Him and Joel have been here for a while, so the mindset has been to complement those guys. I'm finding my footing, but Maxey has been leading the way for sure."

Brown's footing looked firm against Chicago.

Beyond his scoring, he helped the Sixers control the glass, moved the ball within an offense that generated 23 assists during the first half and supplied the physicality Nick Nurse expects from him.

"The dude is tough and he wins," Nurse said. "I'll take that all day long. The degree of difficulty on some of the shots he hit was really amazing. I thought he pounded the glass and got some key rebounds. Makes a lot of winning plays. Man, he's a winner."

Brown spent the first 10 years of his career in Boston. He won a championship there, reached another NBA Finals and grew from a 20-year-old prospect into one of the league's premier two-way wings.

Moving into a new system alongside James, Embiid and Maxey was never going to be seamless.

"I mean, he's fitting in along with all of us," James said. "We're getting better and better. It's not going to happen overnight. He spent his first 10 years in a system in Boston, in the city, so it's going to take some adjustment.

"It takes adjustment for him. It's going to take adjustment for the rest of the guys that joined this franchise as well. But tonight was a great step."

James pointed to Brown's "pressure, his shot-making ability, his rebounding ability" and his professionalism.

Brown's early influence has extended beyond his production.

The Sixers entered Monday with one of the NBA's best half-court defenses. Brown has been one of the group's most persistent voices, stressing communication, preparation and attention to opposing players' tendencies.

"That's the part that I care about the most as a group, not individually," Brown said. "Having a mentality night in and night out, respecting your opponent, respecting the game, making sure that we are executing our coverages, we're being clear in our communication and then we're also taking away tendencies on a night-to-night basis.

"Those things I just explained are over 50 percent of the battle."

Brown understands that maintaining those details across an 82-game schedule will require more than reminders.

"A little bit of accountability," he said. "You learn different guys require different things. How you communicate with each guy may be a little different, but accountability for sure and confrontation if need be.

"The offense is going to be what it's going to be, but our defense has got to be non-negotiable. That's something I say all the time. Non-negotiable. You want to be a good team, defense is non-negotiable."

The Sixers showed both sides of their defensive potential Monday.

They built a double-digit lead during the first half, allowed Chicago to score 36 points in the second quarter and then created separation after halftime. Philadelphia held the Bulls to 20 points in the third quarter before pulling away in the fourth.

Brown did not celebrate their ability to raise their intensity after it slipped.

"I don't like that we have that," he said. "It's good that we have shown the potential, but we've got to keep that switch on. It doesn't work like that where you just flip the switch.

"It can catch up to us and it can bite us against a better team or on a night that we're not being as crisp on offense. It can't be a switch just because we're playing a lesser opponent or whatever the case may be. We've got to make sure that mentality is from the beginning to end. Can't skip any steps."

That urgency accompanies considerable optimism.

Brown said the Sixers enjoy playing together. He loves when James grabs a rebound because "he's like a quarterback," capable of launching an outlet pass or immediately pushing the pace.

The group is learning when to attack, when to move the ball and how to avoid hesitating in its effort to play unselfishly.

"It's a lot of talent, man," Brown said. "We like each other, and we're just kind of building that chemistry of how we can get this thing to a well-oiled machine. I think we're taking steps forward every single day."

The Sixers are 7-1 despite Brown believing those steps remain incomplete. They have won close games, erased sizable deficits and received important contributions from different players.

Brown's performance Monday showed another version of how their pieces can fit.

"We still have a long way to go to being a really, really solid, great team," Brown said. "But we've been able to win some games. We started out the season great, 7-1, and you haven't seen our best version yet.

#2822. Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30

Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers remain the Eastern Conference's sole leader.

They earned a 112-106 road win over the Pistons on Wednesday night to move to 8-1 on the season and stay at the top of the standings. Detroit fell to 6-2.

The Sixers last started 8-1 in the 2023-24 season, which was Nick Nurse's first as the team's head coach.

Jaylen Brown scored a season-high 30 points and pulled down seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid had 26 points and a season-best 15 rebounds. LeBron James posted 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Tyrese Maxey added 19 points and seven assists.

The Pistons' leading scorers were Duncan Robinson with 27 points and Cade Cunningham with 26.

The Sixers were down Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pistons' injured players included Jalen Duren (right hamstring strain) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion).

Nurse told reporters in Detroit he thinks "it'll be another 10 to 12 days before they kind of clear (Barlow) for getting on the court to see where he is," according to Sixers Wire's Ky Carlin.

The Sixers will visit the Cavaliers on Friday night. Here are observations on their victory over Detroit:

Embiid assisted the Sixers' first basket with a sharp pass out of a double team. He saw Brown's cut along the baseline and dished to him for a layup.

Detroit ran several double drag screen actions early, forcing Embiid to defend on the perimeter. The Pistons started 7 for 11 from the floor and took a 17-11 edge on a Robinson three-pointer.

The Sixers then made a 10-0 run and Embiid was right in the middle of it. He converted a put-back layup after a pretty high-low feed from James. Embiid hit two foul shots to give the Sixers the lead. The team raised its defensive level and Detroit's offense grew frigid.

Embiid was very good on the glass in the first half, grabbing eight rebounds. The Sixers had an excellent rebounding game as a team, limiting the Pistons to four offensive boards over 48 minutes.

Embiid didn't break out of his early-season three-point shooting slump, going 0 for 3. He's 3 for 26 (11.5 percent) on the season and hasn't made a three since the Sixers' second game.

Late in the second quarter, Embiid got into a dead-ball dust-up with Tolu Smith. After an officials' review, Embiid was assessed a technical foul for "initiating" the altercation.

Playing on his 26th birthday, Maxey missed his first four field goals and was scoreless until he hit a floater with 31.5 seconds left in the first quarter.

Brown picked up the scoring slack, tallying 10 points in the first on 4-for-6 shooting and hitting a deep, buzzer-beating three to put the Sixers up 29-21. He produced at all three levels, chose smart spots to attack and looked comfortable in the rhythm of the Sixers' offense.

Meanwhile, James did his usuall stellar work as a passer. He assisted two Adem Bona slams in the second quarter and constantly spotted open teammates. Nurse rewarded Bona's strong opening stint, playing him for a lengthy stretch.

Brown swished a corner triple to extend the Sixers' lead to 48-31. With a 3-for-5 night, Brown is at 45.7 percent from long distance so far this season. It wouldn't be surprising at all if Brown's three-point shooting improved from last season's 34.7 percent clip. With such an abundance of star power, the Sixers' hope will be that everyone gets regular open looks beyond the arc throughout the year.

As for Maxey, he sat with 3:26 left in the second quarter after being whistled for his third foul. Even with a mere two points from Maxey, the Sixers entered halftime holding a 14-point advantage.

The Pistons played better basketball to begin the third quarter.

Following a John Collins alley-oop jam, Nurse called timeout with his team's lead down to single digits. The Pistons' offense sustained some success, but the Sixers prevented a sustained run.

Embiid played an especially physical, aggressive third quarter. He tipped in his own miss and Maxey then sunk a three to make the Sixers' lead 84-68. They were up as many as 17 points in the third.

Embiid sat out the fourth quarter Monday night for the Sixers' win over the Bulls and said he was on a minutes restriction (25) because of his right foot plantar fasciitis. He played the fourth period against the Pistons and logged 33 minutes. Bona went back to the locker room early in the fourth. Nurse told reporters postgame that Bona had "neck soreness."

Detroit did not let the Sixers coast to victory.

Robinson drained a three. Cunningham made a pair of free throws and drove in for a layup that cut the Pistons' deficit to 106-102.

The Sixers halted the Pistons' run before anything disastrous was on the table. Brown blocked a Cunningham three-point try, Embiid knocked down two foul shots, and the East's No. 1 early-season team improved to 4-0 on the road.

#2820. NHL Rumours: Montreal Canadiens Interested in Simon Edvinsson and Dylan Larkin

NHL rumours continue to circulate about the Detroit Red Wings and how they will deal with the trade requests from Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson. On Wednesday's DFO Insider Podcast with Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta, a new rumour was added that features the Montreal Canadiens. Let's get into the details.

Rumour: On the DFO Insider Podcast, Marek and Pagnotta were discussing the current situation in Detroit. With respect to Larkin, Pagnotta said that the player's camp want to work from his 10-team trade list, while the Red Wings feel they can get a better offer from another team, such as Montreal or Buffalo. Pagnotta said he expects the matter to be settled by American Thanksgiving, because one of the parties concedes. Pagnotta also said that "as much as Montreal has been linked to and have significant interest in Larkin, there is also a lot of interest in Edvinsson from Montreal's side".

Analysis: Montreal's interest in Larkin is well documented. It has also been widely reported that Larkin has a 10-team trade list that the Canadiens are not on. Beyond this, even if the player would agree, the asking price from Detroit has been prohibitive. Unless Larkin has a change of heart and accepts a trade to Montreal, and the parties can agree on a trade package, there will be no deal. The interest in Edvinsson is new information, and somewhat surprising considering the depth the Canadiens have on the left side.

Dec 17, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin (71) skates with the puck defended by Utah Mammoth defenseman Mikhail Sergachev (98) in the second period at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images

The NHL rumours connecting the Habs and Larkin will not die down until a trade is finalized. It is no secret that the Montreal Canadiens covet another top six forward, and a centre might be preferred. It's also no secret that their preference is to hold on to top prospect Michael Hage, but for the perfect player, perhaps they would entertain trading him. The unknown is whether the Habs see Larkin as that perfect player.

The Red Wings seem to think teams that are not on the list, like Montreal, are prepared to offer better packages than the 10 teams on the list. This is not a mystery. The few teams on Larkin's list that can actually make a trade for him know they are still in the driver's seat until Larkin expands his list.

From the player's perspective, Larkin's camp believes they have been reasonable in offering up 10 teams, and that the interim general manager in Detroit, Shawn Horcoff, should be able to make a fair deal from that list.

As Pagnotta noted, this cannot go on forever, and eventually one party will have to concede to the other. What that means for Montreal depends on who wins the standoff, but the NHL rumours are unlikely to stop as long as Detroit keeps sending scouts to the Canadiens games.

The pressure on the Detroit Red Wings to either sign or trade Simon Edvinsson is a little more concrete. December 1st is the deadline for teams to sign outstanding restricted free agents, and time is running out for Detroit. With Edvinsson's pedigree being that of a certain top-four defender who will likely grow into a top pair role, there is no shortage of interest. Montreal's interest comes as a bit of a surprise.

The Habs have a number of left shot defenders in Lane Hutson, Mike Matheson, Kaiden Guhle, Arber Xhekaj, and Adam Engstrom, just to name the players currently on the roster. The right side is where you would expect them to target. But perhaps they see Edvinsson as the kind of player that upgrades your roster so significantly that they are prepared to figure out the other details after the fact.

The Detroit Red Wings are at the centre of NHL rumours, and will continue to be until the cases of Larkin and Edvinsson have been resolved. Both are players that can become part of a team's core for years to come, and the Red Wings are under pressure to get a strong return. The Montreal Canadiens are uniquely positioned with roster players, prospects and picks that they can move to obtain an upgrade, and they will continue to be linked to Detroit until these deals are done.
